title: Class Soup
lead: Today we will cook a real soup together! Let’s look at the recipe. This is the list of food that we will need and also the directions.
alt: Companion illustration of an adult and child looking at a picture recipe with colorful vegetables and cooking steps; this is not the class’s selected recipe.
notes: Source and Teaching Materials

This is the real-food Class Soup activity, distinct from the pretend soup in Dramatic Play. Use your selected recipe and the physical materials below. The on-screen companion illustration shows an adult and child looking at a picture recipe; it is not the class’s selected recipe, a required ingredient list, or a photograph of this class. The source’s Bryce, Camilla, and Yoshi example illustrates taking turns and does not identify children in this class.
Purpose
Children cook real soup together.
Big Ideas
Color is a property of many natural and human-made things. There is an infinite variety of colors.
Guiding Question
What colors do we notice all around us? How do colors provide information?
Family Engagement

Invite families and caregivers to share their favorite soup. This could be a recipe, or photograph, an herb packet, or even donated empty food containers (e.g., an empty box of noodles). If interested, invite family members to share their expertise by coming in to talk about the food or demonstrating how to cook the food. Invite caregivers to come into cook soup together with the children.
Vocabulary
gather: to collect things
ingredients: things that are mixed together to make a dish
mix: put different things together
prepare: to make something
recipe: a list of ingredients and directions for making food
stir: to mix by moving a spoon/ladle in a circle
Materials
simple recipe Select a soup recipe that children can easily follow. There is an example in the back of Soup Day or invite families to share a favorite recipe.
chart paper and markers Transfer the recipe onto chart paper. Where possible make the recipe visual (e.g., next to the “6 cups of broth”, draw out 6 cups).

ingredients to make the soup To make the cooking process easier, prepare some of the ingredients ahead of time. And leave some of the preparation for the children (e.g, children can help wash and cut vegetables)
cooking implements such as a large pot, colanders, child-safe cutting tools, ladles
As an alternative to soup, the class may prepare a fruit or vegetable salad.
Note: be aware of any food allergies/preferences.
Intro to Centers
In the story Green is a Chile Pepper/Red is a Dragon we noticed the many colors of different foods. What foods are special to your family?
Invite 1-2 responses.

In Soup Day, the child and mom worked together to cook soup. And you are making soup in Dramatic Play! A soup is made by cooking ingredients slowly in a big pot. In Soup Day, they used ingredients such as carrots, celery, and mushrooms. So many different colors!
Today we will cook a real soup together! Let’s look at the recipe. This is the list of food that we will need and also the directions.
Show recipe on chart paper. Point to the sections of the recipe while talking through it.

I already gathered the ingredients, or the foods that we will need to make the soup. Let’s look at the ingredient list: _____ [list ingredients]. First we will wash the ingredients and chop them into small pieces. Then we will stir them all together in our pot and add seasonings, like salt, pepper, and herbs, for extra flavor. We will make everything very hot so that it cooks all the ingredients. How might our soup change after we add heat to it?
Harvest responses from children.
When we’re finished, we can taste the soup we cooked together today during lunch.
During Centers

Children first wash their hands and cook soup together. As small groups join the Science and Engineering Center, share what step of the recipe is being followed. Use ordinal language (first, second, third) while following the recipe. Invite children to take turns completing steps of the recipe (e.g., First Bryce will pour in the milk; second, Camilla will add the flour; third Yoshi will stir the ingredients with a spoon.).

Encourage children to notice the characteristics of the ingredients, such as the color, texture, smell or amount before cooking. Then ask how they think the ingredients might change when we add heat to them

Sample the warm finished soup together during snack or lunch. Ask children about how the color, texture, and smell of the ingredients changed. Consider making another batch for your Color Party at the end of the unit.
Differentiation Ideas
Use the visual soup recipe connected to Soup Day (see Dramatic Play, U2 W1 ) to support children with making a soup.
Use the cooking topic board (see Dramatic Play, U1 W1) to support children with communication as they prepare a soup with real ingredients.

Break down the experience over several days, one day each for: exploring the vegetables textures and names, washing the vegetables, cutting the vegetables/making observations about the insides, mixing the vegetables and cooking the soup.
Use the steps that are appropriate for your classroom.
Partially cook vegetables (e.g., in a microwave) to make them easier to cut.
Ensure children know the difference between pretend and real ingredients. Practice with the pretend ingredients before using the real ingredients.
Facilitation
How are our ingredients similar to or different from the ones in the book, _____(Soup Day or Green is a Chile Pepper or Red is a Dragon)?
Which step in the recipe comes first/next? How do you know?
What foods are special to you and your family?
Have you eaten soup with your family before? What kind was it?
What do we need to do first (second, third) to prepare our soup?
What colors do you see in this soup?
Why do you like this soup?
How does the soup change when we add heat to it?
Standards
PreK-LS1-3(MA). Use their five senses in their exploration and play to gather information.
PreK-PS1-4 (MA) Recognize through investigation that physical objects and materials can change under different circumstances.
Science and Engineering Practice 3: Planning and Carrying Out Investigations
SL.PK.1b. Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
